tagline: Key to key on an old railroad bed, down to zero.
intro: Over the Jewfish Creek Bridge, US 1 leaves the mainland behind and goes island to island, 110 miles across 43 keys to Mile Marker 0 in Old Town Key West. Much of it rides the bed of Henry Flagler's Overseas Railroad, finished in 1912 and wrecked by the Labor Day hurricane of 1935. The railway could not afford to rebuild, so the state bought the roadbed and bridges and made a highway of them.

The mile markers count down toward Key West, and outside Key West and Marathon the street addresses go by them. The designated corridor reaches five miles into the water on either side, where manatees and green sea turtles live or pass through.

moments.title: Islamorada
moments.text: The 1935 hurricane struck the village almost head-on. At mile marker 82 a memorial holds the ashes of more than 300 of its victims.

moments.title: Pigeon Key
moments.text: The old Seven Mile Bridge, closed to cars, runs out to the five-acre island where Flagler's railroad kept a work camp. When it carried cars, its guardrails were the old track, painted white.

moments.title: Big Pine Key
moments.text: Most of the Key deer, the smallest deer in North America, now live on this one island. They feed along the roadsides and are harder to avoid at night.
